sentences.en: Okay, with all that in mind, without further ado, what are we talking about today?
sentences.zh: 好了，考虑到这一切，废话不多说，我们今天谈论什么呢？

sentences.en: Because we're not talking about my book, we're talking about something very, very different.
sentences.zh: 因为我们不是在谈论我的书，我们是在谈论一些非常、非常不同的东西。

sentences.en: We're talking about the psychology of pre-menstrual syndrome, PMs.
sentences.zh: 我们正在谈论经前综合症（PMS）的心理学。

sentences.en: We are talking about this black box of hormones and mood swings and rage and acne and so many other things that impact a whole lot of people,
sentences.zh: 我们正在谈论这个充满荷尔蒙、情绪波动、愤怒、痤疮以及许多其他影响着许多人的黑匣子，

sentences.en: but which I don't think I even really understood until a year ago.
sentences.zh: 但我认为直到一年前我才真正理解它。

sentences.en: You know, I've had my period since I was 13, but something that I've noticed is that we actually know very little about our bodies on an individual scale.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我从13岁起就开始来月经了，但我注意到的一点是，我们实际上对自己身体的个体层面知之甚少。

sentences.en: There are very few guides or times when somebody is going to sit down with you and just say, this is what's happening at your body at certain times of the month.
sentences.zh: 很少有指南或时刻会有人坐下来告诉你，你的身体在每个月的特定时间发生了什么。

sentences.en: This is why you feel this way.
sentences.zh: 这就是你为什么会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: This is what your hormones do.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的荷尔蒙在做什么。

sentences.en: This is how they influence mood.
sentences.zh: 这就是它们如何影响情绪。

sentences.en: This is what is actually happening in this vessel that you have.
sentences.zh: 这就是你所拥有的这个躯体里真正发生的事情。

sentences.en: You know, we're just expected to deal with it, even when it impacts our well-being, without ever actually having the information that could actually make it better.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们只是被期望去应对它，即使它影响了我们的健康，却从未真正获得能让情况好转的信息。

sentences.en: But today, I want to hopefully provide that guide to you around PMS and PMDD so that you can know yourself and know your body better
sentences.zh: 但今天，我希望能为你提供一份关于PMS和PMDD（经前不悦症）的指南，这样你就能更好地了解自己和你的身体，

sentences.en: and know how it interacts with your psychology because learning this in your 20s, you know, it's such an important time for you to start taking these kinds of things seriously
sentences.zh: 并了解它如何与你的心理相互作用，因为在20多岁时学习这些，你知道，这是你开始认真对待这些事情的重要时期，

sentences.en: and to start really feeling in touch with your body.
sentences.zh: 并开始真正感受到与身体的联系。

sentences.en: And it's a great time to be reintroduced to so many ideas and concepts that we haven't even really spoken about since puberty, but are a constant reality for us.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重新接触许多我们自青春期以来就没怎么谈论过，但却是我们持续现实的概念的好时机。

sentences.en: So, yes, we're talking PMS, we're talking PMDD, and we're talking periods,
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们在谈论PMS，我们在谈论PMDD，我们在谈论月经，

sentences.en: specifically the psychology behind why that period of time before our period takes such a toll and what's creating that,
sentences.zh: 特别是月经前那段时间为什么会造成如此大的影响，以及是什么造成了这种影响的心理学背景，

sentences.en: but also how to manage those fluctuations, the frustration, maybe even the shame we feel, the mental impact, the stigma,
sentences.zh: 但也包括如何管理这些波动、挫败感，甚至是我们感到的羞耻感、心理影响、污名化，

sentences.en: and also some more niche questions like, should you break up with your partner during your luteal phase?
sentences.zh: 还有一些更小众的问题，比如，你应该在黄体期和伴侣分手吗？

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 大概不应该。

sentences.en: Is PMS a good defense for murder?
sentences.zh: PMS是谋杀的有效辩护理由吗？

sentences.en: Also, no, we've got, like, so many niche things to talk about.
sentences.zh: 答案也是否定的，我们还有很多小众话题要聊。

sentences.en: Hopefully, I have you hooked, but I am going to stop rambling now and just get into the science and the psychology of PMs.
sentences.zh: 希望我能吸引住你，但我现在要停止闲聊，直接进入PMS的科学和心理学领域。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Okay, so our bodies and hormones and periods are so complex and seriously different for everyone.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们的身体、荷尔蒙和月经是如此复杂，对每个人来说都截然不同。

sentences.en: You know, I have never met two individuals who have the same experiences with their uteruses.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我从未见过两个人在子宫体验上完全相同的人。

sentences.en: So, if you experience PMS, it's going to be different as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你经历PMS，情况也会有所不同。

sentences.en: But with that in mind, with that caveat being said, let's just start with some really basic factual information about PMs.
sentences.zh: 但考虑到这一点，在有这个前提的情况下，让我们先从关于PMS的一些非常基础的事实信息开始。

sentences.en: Now, we're not going to go too much into the medical side of things because that's not my area of expertise, but the basic explanation of PMS is this.
sentences.zh: 我们不会过多深入医学方面，因为那不是我的专业领域，但PMS的基本解释是这样的。

sentences.en: PMS basically describes a set of symptoms or changes that occur before your period.
sentences.zh: PMS基本上描述了月经前出现的一系列症状或变化。

sentences.en: And it's estimated that about three quarters of people who get their period experience at least one change that would fall under the umbrella of PMS,
sentences.zh: 据估计，大约四分之三来月经的人会经历至少一种属于PMS范畴的变化，

sentences.en: even if it's not noticeable to us.
sentences.zh: 即使我们自己并没有察觉到。

sentences.en: So, let's go through some of these changes because they are both emotional and physical and psychological.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们来看看其中的一些变化，因为它们既是情绪上的，也是生理和心理上的。

sentences.en: I'm going to start with the ones that I would say are seemingly most common.
sentences.zh: 我先从那些我认为似乎最常见的开始说起。

sentences.en: The most common ones are tension and anxiety, a depressed mood, crying spells, bloating, acne,
sentences.zh: 最常见的是紧张和焦虑、情绪低落、哭泣、腹胀、痤疮，

sentences.en: but then also mood swings, irritability, appetite and craving changes, insomnia, fatigue, headaches, poor concentration,
sentences.zh: 但还有情绪波动、易怒、食欲和渴望的变化、失眠、疲劳、头痛、注意力不集中，

sentences.en: change in libido, social withdrawal, just to name a few.
sentences.zh: 性欲改变、社交退缩，仅举几例。

sentences.en: You know, some people even describe wanting to break up with their partner during their luteal phase, right before their period, and they kind of attribute it to their PMs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些人甚至描述说在黄体期，也就是月经前，想和伴侣分手，他们把这归因于PMS。

sentences.en: In fact, it's actually common for people who get their periods to have more concerns about their relationship
sentences.zh: 事实上，来月经的人在月经前对关系的担忧更多是很常见的，

sentences.en: right before they menstruate, because they can be a lot more sensitive or aware of interpersonal probleMs.
sentences.zh: 因为她们可能会变得更加敏感或意识到人际关系中的问题。

sentences.en: I think more irritable in general, and we'll explain why that is, because it's certainly not just because women are too emotional, it's a real hormonal thing.
sentences.zh: 我认为总体上会更易怒，我们会解释为什么会这样，因为这绝对不仅仅是因为女性太情绪化，这是一种真实的荷尔蒙现象。

sentences.en: But a recent study conducted at UCLA did find that women evaluate their relationships differently
sentences.zh: 但加州大学洛杉矶分校（UCLA）最近的一项研究确实发现，女性在周期的不同时间对关系的评价不同，

sentences.en: at different times in their cycle, sometimes even finding their partners less attractive right before their period.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至在月经前觉得伴侣没那么有吸引力。

sentences.en: But that doesn't necessarily mean they want to break up with them or are less committed.
sentences.zh: 但这并不一定意味着她们想分手或投入度降低。

sentences.en: It's just a lot more complicated than that, and it can just create a lot of nuanced feelings.
sentences.zh: 这比那复杂得多，它只会产生很多微妙的情绪。

sentences.en: And if you're someone who has a lot of relationship anxiety, sometimes that time right before your
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个有较多关系焦虑的人，有时在月经前那段时间，

sentences.en: period, it's really important to be aware of the fact that you are going to experience heightened sensitivity and doubts.
sentences.zh: 意识到你将会经历高度敏感和怀疑是非常重要的。

sentences.en: And how can you stay neutral in the face of that, knowing that there's another factor contributing?
sentences.zh: 面对这种情况，你如何保持中立，并知道还有另一个因素在起作用？

sentences.en: We're going to talk about that in a second, but another interesting symptom that I'm sure a lot of us are familiar with is changes in body image.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会讨论这个问题，但另一个我确信我们很多人都很熟悉的有趣症状是身体形象的变化。

sentences.en: Our views towards our bodies change significantly for many women before the period.
sentences.zh: 许多女性在月经前对身体的看法会发生显著变化。

sentences.en: In fact, this probably won't come as a surprise.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这可能并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Our body image and our appraisal of our body typically gets worse.
sentences.zh: 我们的身体形象和对身体的评价通常会变差。

sentences.en: Now, studies have shown this as early as the 80s and 90s, and it's not just because we're bloated.
sentences.zh: 研究早在80年代和90年代就表明了这一点，而且不仅仅是因为我们腹胀。

sentences.en: Obviously, that's a factor.
sentences.zh: 显然，那是一个因素。

sentences.en: It's because body image is a part of our self-concept, and our self-concept is regulated by our brain and to an extent our nervous system and how we're feeling.
sentences.zh: 这是因为身体形象是我们自我概念的一部分，而我们的自我概念受大脑调节，在一定程度上也受神经系统和我们感受的影响。

sentences.en: So when our nervous system is dysregulated because of hormonal changes, our opinion of our self will also change.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们的神经系统因为荷尔蒙变化而失调时，我们对自己的评价也会改变。

sentences.en: For me, I always experience this.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我总是经历这种情况。

sentences.en: I always feel, you know, there's really no better word than like disgusting.
sentences.zh: 我总是觉得，真的没有比“恶心”更好的词了。

sentences.en: Like I feel disgusting and ugly and like a monster right before my period.
sentences.zh: 月经前我感觉自己恶心、丑陋，像个怪物。

sentences.en: And every single time, like on the dot, three days before, I'll be like, wow, I have never
sentences.zh: 而且每次都是这样，准时在三天前，我会想，哇，我从来没有

sentences.en: felt more swollen and I've never felt uglier.
sentences.zh: 感觉这么肿，也从来没有感觉这么丑过。

sentences.en: And I just feel disgusting and like I'm going to feel like this way forever.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己很恶心，好像我会永远这样下去。

sentences.en: And then it's like, oh, bam, I get my period.
sentences.zh: 然后，砰，月经来了。

sentences.en: And it explains it all.
sentences.zh: 一切都解释通了。

sentences.en: And I still, I still have this issue of not being able to put two and two together.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然有这个问题，就是无法把这两件事联系起来。

sentences.en: Like really my body, my lack of body confidence only really comes around the time I get my period.
sentences.zh: 我的身体自信心缺失真的只出现在我来月经的时候。

sentences.en: And it comes almost every single month.
sentences.zh: 而且几乎每个月都会发生。

sentences.en: And yet I'm still surprised when suddenly I feel awful.
sentences.zh: 然而，当我突然感觉糟糕时，我仍然感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I don't know if you can relate, but I do feel like for many of us, we are still shocked by the fact that our bodies and our minds are going to react to the fact that we go through
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否有同感，但我确实觉得我们很多人仍然对我们的身体和思想会对我们所经历的事情做出反应这一事实感到震惊。

sentences.en: an entire life cycle every month.
sentences.zh: 每个月都有一个完整的生命周期。

sentences.en: And seriously, that is what it is.
sentences.zh: 说真的，事实就是如此。

sentences.en: When you get your period, you are at the end of that life cycle.
sentences.zh: 当你来月经时，你就处于那个生命周期的终点。

sentences.en: That's how your entire reproductive system is operating.
sentences.zh: 这就是你整个生殖系统的运作方式。

sentences.en: That is why when you are about to get your period, it does feel like a kind of death.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当你快要来月经时，感觉就像经历了一场死亡。

sentences.en: Like it feels like you're dying.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像你要死了一样。

sentences.en: Do you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: And then once ovulation comes back around, you know, you're practically buzzing because that's like the prime days of your egg's life, you know, and it's all a cycle of rebirth
sentences.zh: 一旦排卵期再次到来，你知道，你几乎会感到兴奋，因为那是卵子生命中最黄金的时期，你知道，这一切都是重生的循环，

sentences.en: and renewal and death and life.
sentences.zh: 是更新、死亡与生命的循环。

sentences.en: And hopefully this explanation makes sense to you.
sentences.zh: 希望这个解释对你来说是有意义的。

sentences.en: But it does just show why PMS can be so debilitating, but also frustrating.
sentences.zh: 但这确实说明了为什么经前综合征（PMS）会让人如此虚弱，同时也令人沮丧。

sentences.en: Sometimes it feels like your body is almost punishing you in a real way.
sentences.zh: 有时感觉你的身体真的在惩罚你。

sentences.en: Like, okay, well, you didn't get pregnant here.
sentences.zh: 就像是，好吧，你这次没怀孕。

sentences.en: This can be your punishment for not doing what we think you should be doing.
sentences.zh: 这就是你没做我们认为你应该做的事情所受的惩罚。

sentences.en: But again, it's all part of that very important cycle of birth and death that are occurring in our bodies, which I think is quite spectacular when you think about it.
sentences.zh: 但再说一次，这都是我们体内发生的非常重要的生与死循环的一部分，当你仔细思考时，我觉得这相当壮观。

sentences.en: I think that's just incredible that that is something that occurs.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实不可思议，这竟然是会发生的事情。

sentences.en: So something else to note, fun fact, maybe not so fun, but PMS symptoms will actually get worse the older we get and the closer we get to menopause and perimenopause.
sentences.zh: 所以还有一点需要注意，一个有趣的事实，也许没那么有趣，但随着我们年龄增长，越接近绝经期和围绝经期，经前综合征的症状实际上会变得更严重。

sentences.en: But once we pass over into menopause, it will stop.
sentences.zh: 但一旦我们进入绝经期，它就会停止。

sentences.en: That approach, though, is when it's going to be at its most intense.
sentences.zh: 不过，在那之前，它会达到最强烈的程度。

sentences.en: And that makes sense because our hormones, they change the older we get and they fluctuate more rapidly.
sentences.zh: 这很有道理，因为随着年龄增长，我们的荷尔蒙会发生变化，波动也会更加剧烈。

sentences.en: Suddenly, the closer we get to menopause due to this decline in ovarian function.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，由于卵巢功能衰退，我们离绝经期越来越近。

sentences.en: But a lot of individuals have spoken about this, have spoken about how the older they got, the more they felt that they were sensitive to these hormonal changes.
sentences.zh: 但很多人都谈到过这一点，谈到随着年龄增长，他们感觉自己对这些荷尔蒙变化变得更加敏感。

sentences.en: Maybe that's something you can relate to.
sentences.zh: 也许你能感同身受。

sentences.en: You know, the first 10 years of you getting your period, you never noticed it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，刚来月经的前十年，你从未注意到它。

sentences.en: And now suddenly there are these emotional parts of this process that you never had to deal with before.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这个过程中突然出现了你以前从未处理过的情绪问题。

sentences.en: OK, so there's just some basic information about PMs.
sentences.zh: 好了，以上就是关于经前综合征的一些基本信息。

sentences.en: Let's talk about something else.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈别的。

sentences.en: Let's talk about PMS's, I don't know, angrier sister, premenstrual dysphoric disorder, PMDD.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈经前综合征的，我不知道，更愤怒的姐妹，经前烦躁障碍，即 PMDD。

sentences.en: So PMDD is basically a severe form of PMs.
sentences.zh: 所以 PMDD 基本上是经前综合征的一种严重形式。

sentences.en: It shows up a lot less in the population around, you know, estimates are two to five percent, but it is extremely debilitating.
sentences.zh: 它在人群中的出现率要低得多，你知道，估计在百分之二到百分之五之间，但它极其令人虚弱。

sentences.en: A lot of people who have PMDD describe it as being like a switch that gets flicked in their brain and suddenly in the week or, you know, two weeks before their period, instantly
sentences.zh: 许多患有 PMDD 的人将其描述为大脑中被拨动了一个开关，突然在月经前的一周或两周，瞬间，

sentences.en: it's like their whole body has been switched with someone else's in a second.
sentences.zh: 就像他们的整个身体在瞬间被换成了别人的。

sentences.en: You know, they will go from sitting at the dinner table being completely content and peaceful
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们前一秒还坐在餐桌旁，完全满足和平静，

sentences.en: and happy one second and then in a click of their fingers, they feel overwhelming rage.
sentences.zh: 快乐地吃着饭，然后弹指之间，他们就感到了无法抑制的愤怒。

sentences.en: They feel paranoia, frustration, deep sadness, like anxiety that won't go away and can't be improved and it feels awful and terrible.
sentences.zh: 他们感到多疑、沮丧、深深的悲伤，就像挥之不去且无法缓解的焦虑，感觉糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: And then just as quickly as it started, it's over.
sentences.zh: 然后，它开始得有多快，结束得就有多快。

sentences.en: You know, I actually saw someone describe PMDD in their case as like a temporary psychosis each month.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我确实看到有人描述他们患 PMDD 的情况就像每个月经历一次短暂的精神病发作。

sentences.en: You know, it's a scary and terrifying thing for them and for many, many people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这对他们以及许多许多人来说是一件可怕且令人恐惧的事情。

sentences.en: And because of that, sometimes it can lead to a misdiagnosis where there are cases of people
sentences.zh: 正因如此，有时它会导致误诊，有些病例中，人们

sentences.en: being diagnosed with very extreme mental health conditions that they don't actually have,
sentences.zh: 被诊断出患有非常极端的心理健康疾病，而实际上他们并没有，

sentences.en: but the intensity of their PMDD symptoms are such that doctors feel like there are no other explanations.
sentences.zh: 但他们的 PMDD 症状强度之大，以至于医生觉得没有其他解释了。

sentences.en: Nowadays, PMD is actually classified as a psychiatric disorder in the DSM-5.
sentences.zh: 如今，PMDD 实际上在《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》第五版（DSM-5）中被归类为精神障碍。

sentences.en: It's under the umbrella of depressive disorders.
sentences.zh: 它属于抑郁障碍的范畴。

sentences.en: So you can get a formal diagnosis if you wish, but it is definitely a struggle identifying whether it's PMDD or some other form of condition.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你愿意，可以获得正式诊断，但要确定它是 PMDD 还是其他形式的疾病，确实是一场挣扎。

sentences.en: And a lot of individuals have explained to me that actually before they were diagnosed with
sentences.zh: 许多人向我解释说，实际上在他们被诊断出

sentences.en: PMDD, they were diagnosed with anxiety, with schizophrenia, with depression.
sentences.zh: PMDD 之前，他们曾被诊断出患有焦虑症、精神分裂症、抑郁症。

sentences.en: And then finally someone said, do you think it's this?
sentences.zh: 直到最后有人问，你觉得是这个吗？

sentences.en: And they had their answer.
sentences.zh: 他们才得到了答案。

sentences.en: So you might be thinking at this stage, well, is it really all that different from depression or bipolar, how can we tell them?
sentences.zh: 所以你现在可能在想，好吧，它真的和抑郁症或双相情感障碍有那么大区别吗？我们该如何区分它们？

sentences.en: Do they really need a different diagnosis?
sentences.zh: 它们真的需要不同的诊断吗？

sentences.en: And yes, they are very, very different because with PMDD, symptoms of depression, of anxiety,
sentences.zh: 是的，它们非常、非常不同，因为对于 PMDD，抑郁、焦虑、

sentences.en: of BPD, of whatever other condition of which there is a similarity, they are only present when you are at a specific stage of your cycle.
sentences.zh: 边缘性人格障碍（BPD）或其他任何有相似之处的疾病的症状，只有当你处于周期的特定阶段时才会出现。

sentences.en: But they will almost completely disappear afterwards.
sentences.zh: 但它们之后几乎会完全消失。

sentences.en: Yes, sometimes an individual may be struggling with the aftermath of what occurred during that
sentences.zh: 是的，有时个人可能会在这一周发生的事情之后感到挣扎，

sentences.en: week, and they may feel like they have to repair some damages, or they're just so tired from how intense everything was.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会觉得必须修复一些损害，或者只是因为一切都太强烈而感到疲惫不堪。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that their symptoms are lasting for the entire four weeks, which means that they are never really in a period of depression or anxiety long enough.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着他们的症状持续了整整四周，这意味着他们从未真正处于足够长时间的抑郁或焦虑期中，

sentences.en: If it's coming from PMDD for them to be classified with anything but PMDD.
sentences.zh: 如果这是由 PMDD 引起的，他们就不会被归类为除 PMDD 以外的任何疾病。

sentences.en: Now, I want to talk about this because I think it's important to note.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想谈谈这个，因为我认为指出这一点很重要。

sentences.en: Some people have suggested that premenstrual dysphoric disorder shouldn't be classified as
sentences.zh: 有些人认为经前烦躁障碍不应该被归类为

sentences.en: a psychiatric disorder because it's just pathologizing normal hormonal fluctuations, and it makes women seem crazy.
sentences.zh: 精神障碍，因为它只是将正常的荷尔蒙波动病理化，让女性看起来像疯子。

sentences.en: And when that debate was around and coming up, there were hundreds and hundreds of letters written by doctors, OBGYNs, psychiatrists, psychologists behind whether or not it should
sentences.zh: 当那场辩论出现时，有数百封由医生、妇产科医生、精神科医生、心理学家写的信，讨论它是否

sentences.en: or shouldn't have been included.
sentences.zh: 应该或不应该被纳入其中。

sentences.en: Some of the arguments are very valid.
sentences.zh: 其中一些论点是非常有道理的。

sentences.en: Like, you know, some feminist scholars, they did say it could be used to silence women.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道，一些女性主义学者确实说过，它可能被用来让女性噤声。

sentences.en: It could feed into, like, a hysteria, a traditional hysteria mindset.
sentences.zh: 它可能助长一种歇斯底里，一种传统的歇斯底里心态。

sentences.en: Some people would say there wasn't enough differentiation.
sentences.zh: 有些人会说区分度不够。

sentences.en: But you know what?
sentences.zh: 但你知道吗？

sentences.en: The level of hormonal fluctuations needed to occur to make someone suicidal or unable to leave bed or to keep a job is not normal.
sentences.zh: 导致一个人产生自杀念头、无法下床或无法保住工作的荷尔蒙波动水平是不正常的。

sentences.en: That's not pathologizing something normal.
sentences.zh: 那不是将正常事物病理化。

sentences.en: And a diagnosis is not only validating, but it is a way to get the help you need.
sentences.zh: 诊断不仅是一种确认，也是获得所需帮助的一种途径。

sentences.en: It helps people also feel seen and acknowledged by the medical community because they have some kind of label that feels respected.
sentences.zh: 它还能帮助人们感到被医疗界看到和认可，因为他们有了一种感觉受到尊重的标签。

sentences.en: And if we can have a formal diagnosis, we can actually start seeing the true prevalence of
sentences.zh: 如果我们能有正式的诊断，我们就能真正开始看到 PMDD 的真实患病率，

sentences.en: PMDD, which also assists in increased research funding, increased awareness, which is really, really essential.
sentences.zh: 这也助于增加研究资金，提高认识，这真的、真的非常重要。

sentences.en: And given how little attention female health gets in general, like, there are more studies done on male baldness than PCOS and endometriosis combined.
sentences.zh: 考虑到女性健康总体上受到的关注如此之少，比如，关于男性脱发的研究比多囊卵巢综合征（PCOS）和子宫内膜异位症加起来还要多。

sentences.en: Like, I think we could do with a little bit more visibility for female health concerns.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们确实需要让女性健康问题获得更多关注。

sentences.en: PMDD and PMS, just to say this one last time, though, they are different.
sentences.zh: 最后再说一次，PMDD 和 PMS 是不同的。

sentences.en: They are very different.
sentences.zh: 它们非常不同。

sentences.en: And PMDD is a lot more extreme.
sentences.zh: 而且 PMDD 要极端得多。

sentences.en: So if PMS was in the DSM, I would understand why people have issues.
sentences.zh: 所以如果 PMS 被列入 DSM，我会理解为什么人们会有异议。

sentences.en: But PMDD is a serious condition.
sentences.zh: 但 PMDD 是一种严重的疾病。

sentences.en: PMS is as well.
sentences.zh: PMS 也是。

sentences.en: But PMDD in particular does require a lot of additional assistance.
sentences.zh: 但 PMDD 特别需要大量的额外帮助。

sentences.en: So I think having a proper diagnosis means that a lot of women will no longer have to have the experience of going to the doctor saying, this is how my life feels.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为拥有一个正确的诊断意味着许多女性将不再需要经历去看医生时说，我的生活感觉就是这样。

sentences.en: It feels like everything is falling apart in this cyclical way.
sentences.zh: 感觉一切都在以这种周期性的方式分崩离析。

sentences.en: And people just assuming, oh, you're just PMSing.
sentences.zh: 而人们只是想当然地说，哦，你只是经前综合征发作了。

sentences.en: Like, just push through it.
sentences.zh: 就像，挺过去就好了。

sentences.en: Take a bath.
sentences.zh: 泡个澡吧。

sentences.en: As if PMS in itself is something that's always going to be easily manageable.
sentences.zh: 好像 PMS 本身就是一种总是很容易处理的事情一样。

sentences.en: So there's one more term I need to introduce here that's separate from PMS and PMDD.
sentences.zh: 所以这里我还需要引入一个术语，它与 PMS 和 PMDD 是分开的。

sentences.en: And it's called premenstrual exacerbation.
sentences.zh: 它被称为经前加重（Premenstrual Exacerbation）。

sentences.en: So if you have an existing mental health condition, like depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你已经患有某种心理健康疾病，比如抑郁症、焦虑症、双相情感障碍，

sentences.en: even something like ADHD, you may notice that your symptoms or conditions get worse in the lead up to your period compared to what you're accustomed to.
sentences.zh: 甚至像多动症（ADHD）这样的疾病，你可能会注意到，与你习惯的情况相比，你的症状或疾病在月经前夕会变得更糟。

sentences.en: Suddenly, you know, your anxiety level is at a 10.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，你知道，你的焦虑水平达到了 10 分。

sentences.en: You feel empty.
sentences.zh: 你感到空虚。

sentences.en: Psychotic symptoms may even worsen as well.
sentences.zh: 精神病性症状甚至也可能加重。

sentences.en: It's not that your symptoms are only occurring during that week.
sentences.zh: 并不是说你的症状只在那一周出现。

sentences.en: They're always present, unlike PMDD.
sentences.zh: 它们一直存在，这与 PMDD 不同。

sentences.en: It's just that just before your period, they get so much worse and it becomes so much harder to deal with.
sentences.zh: 只是在月经前，它们变得严重得多，处理起来也变得困难得多。

sentences.en: So now that we're across these three distinct terms and conditions, let's go right back to
sentences.zh: 现在我们已经了解了这三个不同的术语和疾病，让我们回到

sentences.en: PMS and talk about the why.
sentences.zh: PMS，谈谈原因。

sentences.en: What is responsible for the psychological changes like sudden irritation, like trouble concentrating, like anxiety, brain fog, and then the secondary impact of shame.
sentences.zh: 是什么导致了心理变化，比如突然的烦躁、注意力不集中、焦虑、脑雾，以及随之而来的羞耻感？

sentences.en: And feeling like any kind of visible emotion will have you taken less seriously or respected less.
sentences.zh: 并且感觉任何可见的情绪都会让你被轻视或尊重减少。

sentences.en: Where does this come from?
sentences.zh: 这从何而来？

sentences.en: So there's two hormones we need to be really familiar with here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有两种我们需要非常熟悉的荷尔蒙。

sentences.en: And you've probably already heard of them, of course, estrogen and progesterone.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经听说过它们了，当然，雌激素和孕激素。

sentences.en: Very, very common.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常普遍。

sentences.en: You've probably heard of them when it comes to your birth control, actually, because estrogen and progesterone, well, essentially, they're primarily responsible for reproduction.
sentences.zh: 你可能在谈到避孕时听说过它们，实际上，因为雌激素和孕激素，嗯，本质上，它们主要负责生殖。

sentences.en: For, you know, puberty, for pregnancy, if you do get pregnant, for menopause, for your period, for your cycle.
sentences.zh: 为了，你知道，青春期、怀孕（如果你怀孕了）、绝经期、月经、你的周期。

sentences.en: And wherever you are in your period will determine the level of either of these hormones.
sentences.zh: 无论你处于月经周期的哪个阶段，都会决定这两种荷尔蒙的水平。

sentences.en: So during ovulation, estrogen is typically very high, which contributes to why your skin is glowing, why your hair is radiant, why you feel incredible, because more estrogen
sentences.zh: 所以在排卵期间，雌激素通常非常高，这有助于解释为什么你的皮肤在发光，为什么你的头发有光泽，为什么你感觉棒极了，因为更多的雌激素

sentences.en: means greater chances of getting pregnant.
sentences.zh: 意味着怀孕的机会更大。

sentences.en: So biologically, you want to attract a mate.
sentences.zh: 所以从生物学上讲，你想吸引配偶。

sentences.en: After ovulation, though, progesterone levels rise sharply, while estrogen dips, leading to a lot of physiological and neurobiological changes.
sentences.zh: 然而，排卵后，孕激素水平急剧上升，而雌激素下降，导致许多生理和神经生物学变化。

sentences.en: So researchers have shown that particularly less progesterone, in particular, does change how our brain operates and feels.
sentences.zh: 研究人员已经表明，特别是孕激素的减少，确实改变了我们大脑的运作和感受方式。

sentences.en: Particularly, it changes how we process and regulate levels of serotonin in the brain.

sentences.zh: 有更多的选择，安排一个时间去了解其中的一些，听听别人对你的状况有什么看法，

sentences.zh: 甚至仅仅是让你所经历的一切得到认可，这都非常、非常重要。

sentences.en: Some final two tips.
sentences.zh: 最后两个小建议。

sentences.en: If you have a partner, invite them to share your period app details or invite them to follow along for you, I don't know, what is it?
sentences.zh: 如果你有伴侣，邀请他们分享你的经期应用程序详情，或者邀请他们关注你的，我不知道，那叫什么？

sentences.en: Join your cycle app.
sentences.zh: 加入你的周期应用程序。

sentences.en: Join your cycle app so they can see peaks and troughs, understand when to bring up arguments,
sentences.zh: 加入你的周期应用程序，这样他们就能看到高峰和低谷，了解什么时候提出争论，

sentences.en: when to bring up small things better for both of you so that you're not constantly in a state of conflict.
sentences.zh: 什么时候提出小事对你们双方都更好，这样你们就不会一直处于冲突状态。

sentences.en: I also sometimes do this with my friends.
sentences.zh: 我有时也会和朋友这样做。

sentences.en: You just understand each other better.
sentences.zh: 你们只是更了解彼此了。

sentences.en: You know what the other person needs.
sentences.zh: 你知道对方需要什么。

sentences.en: You can mediate and moderate conversation and expectations and communication and plans so much better when you do just have a more in-depth understanding of what everyone's current emotional capacity and emotional state is like.
sentences.zh: 当你对每个人的当前情绪容量和情绪状态有更深入的了解时，你就能更好地调解和缓和对话、期望、沟通和计划。

sentences.en: And have empathy for yourself.
sentences.zh: 对自己多一点同理心。

sentences.en: You know, your body is so complex.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你的身体非常复杂。

sentences.en: Like, it's one of the most complex things to exiSt.
sentences.zh: 它是世界上最复杂的存在之一。

sentences.en: And there is nobody in the world who can possibly understand every single reaction and thing that goes on below the surface that you are forced to feel.
sentences.zh: 世界上没有人能完全理解你被迫感受到的、在表面之下发生的每一个反应和事情。

sentences.en: Like, PMS dials every single tiny reaction up to 100 and has you feel them all at once.
sentences.zh: 就像PMS会将每一个微小的反应放大到100倍，让你同时感受到它们。

sentences.en: And it's tricky and it's hard.
sentences.zh: 这很棘手，也很艰难。

sentences.en: But it's also something that others are going through and you can find the light in it.
sentences.zh: 但这也是其他人正在经历的事情，你可以在其中找到光明。

sentences.en: There are so many more resources, so many more ways and opportunities to be open in our communication, to talk about it and to make this condition, both PMS and PMDD,
sentences.zh: 现在有更多的资源，更多的方式和机会来开放沟通，谈论它，并使这种状况，无论是PMS还是PMDD，

sentences.en: more visible and not a weakness.
sentences.zh: 变得更加可见，而不是一种弱点。

sentences.en: Just an addition to our lives that we have to navigate as expertly as possible.
sentences.zh: 这只是我们生活中必须尽可能专业地去应对的一个附加部分。

sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 今年我对待健康的方式非常不同。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more.
sentences.zh: 我过去非常专注于最大化和做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better.
sentences.zh: 而现在我意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现会好得多。

sentences.en: And that's why I am obsessed with my WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我沉迷于我的WHOOP。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know I'm such a data and information-driven person.
sentences.zh: 真的，伙计们，你们知道我是一个非常注重数据和信息的人。

sentences.en: And I love opening my WHOOP app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day-to-day.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢打开我的WHOOP应用程序，看看我的睡眠、压力、劳损如何与我的情绪、跑步表现以及我每天的感受相关联。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit and I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 我绝不是什么精英运动员，但我确实从中受益匪浅，而且我也真的很喜欢了解更多关于我身体的信息。

sentences.en: And WHOOP also gives me these actionable,

sentences.zh: 个性化的见解，让我变得更有意图，意味着我每天能做出更明智的决定，了解我需要什么，而不是仅仅踩下油门，

sentences.en: going, going, going.
sentences.zh: 不停地、不停地、不停地前进。

sentences.zh: 本周的听众提问太棒了。

sentences.en: They were so amazing.
sentences.zh: 它们太令人惊叹了。

sentences.en: I was very intrigued to dig a little bit deeper into what you guys want to know.
sentences.zh: 我非常有兴趣深入挖掘你们想知道的内容。

sentences.en: We're going to start with this question, which I found so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我们先从这个问题开始，我觉得它非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: How would PMS interact with ADHD?
sentences.zh: 经前综合症（PMS）会如何与多动症（ADHD）相互作用？

sentences.en: So I consulted some really interesting articles about this, specifically a paper from 2023.
sentences.zh: 所以我查阅了一些关于此的非常有趣的文章，特别是一篇2023年的论文。

sentences.en: And what it suggested is that having ADHD and PMS is, and this is literally their words, this is a direct quote from this article, a double whammy.
sentences.zh: 它的建议是，同时患有ADHD和PMS，这是——这真的是他们的原话，这是这篇文章的直接引用——一种“双重打击”。

sentences.en: Whereby, symptoms of ADHD are more likely to increase when estrogen levels drop.
sentences.zh: 即，当雌激素水平下降时，ADHD的症状更有可能加剧。

sentences.en: So right as your period starts and just before.
sentences.zh: 也就是在月经开始时和开始前夕。

sentences.en: In particular, they found two things happen.
sentences.zh: 特别是，他们发现发生了两件事。

sentences.en: There is an increase in approach slash risk-taking behaviors, but more so an increase in avoidance and negative effect.
sentences.zh: 接近/冒险行为有所增加，但更多的是回避和负面情绪的增加。

sentences.en: So negative mood, but also in attention symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 也就是负面情绪，以及注意力不集中症状的增加。

sentences.en: So if you're finding that your ADHD is getting worse before your period, you are not mistaken.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你发现你的ADHD在月经前变得更糟，你并没有错。

sentences.en: It's a real thing.
sentences.zh: 这是真实存在的。

sentences.en: And they also noted, and I'm glad they did, that the pressure to mask your ADHD or appear functional is also a lot more prominent and stronger in women.
sentences.zh: 他们还指出——我很高兴他们指出了这一点——掩盖ADHD或表现得功能正常的压力在女性身上也更为突出和强烈。

sentences.en: And so it sometimes feels that you have to suppress or conceal two things at once.
sentences.zh: 因此，有时你会觉得必须同时压抑或隐藏两件事。

sentences.en: You know, you have to suppress your ADHD symptoms, even though you feel more agitated and you feel like they are stronger.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你必须压抑你的ADHD症状，即使你感到更加烦躁，并且觉得它们更强烈了。

sentences.en: But you also don't want to be seen as overly emotional.
sentences.zh: 但你也不想被视为过于情绪化。

sentences.en: So you have to either consciously or unconsciously ignore your PMS symptoms as well.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须有意识或无意识地忽略你的PMS症状。

sentences.en: I know that probably paints a very bleak picture, but I think that information is so valuable to know because you can just say to yourself, this is not me.
sentences.zh: 我知道这可能描绘了一幅非常凄凉的画面，但我认为这些信息非常有价值，因为你可以对自己说，这不是我个人的问题。

sentences.en: Like, it's not just me.
sentences.zh: 就像，不仅仅是我这样。

sentences.en: It's not because I'm too sensitive or weak or because I lack discipline.
sentences.zh: 这不是因为我太敏感、软弱，或者因为我缺乏纪律。

sentences.en: It's because of this so-called double whammy, this hormonal influence on my mental state and my capacity to pay attention, to focus, to control my impulses.
sentences.zh: 这是因为所谓的“双重打击”，这种荷尔蒙对我的心理状态以及我集中注意力、专注、控制冲动能力的影响。

sentences.en: So I would really recommend reading this article.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的建议阅读这篇文章。

sentences.en: It's called Attention Deficit slash Hyperactivity Disorder and the Menstrual Cycle Theory and Evidence from the Journal of Hormones and Behavior.
sentences.zh: 它发表在《荷尔蒙与行为》杂志上，标题是《注意力缺陷/多动障碍与月经周期：理论与证据》。

sentences.en: It's actually also free access as well.
sentences.zh: 它实际上也是免费获取的。

sentences.en: And if you're a psychology student or someone who accesses a lot of academic papers, you'll know that when something's free, when you have an open access paper,
sentences.zh: 如果你是一名心理学学生，或者经常查阅学术论文的人，你会知道当某样东西是免费的，当你有一篇开放获取的论文时，

sentences.en: it's like a dream come true.
sentences.zh: 那简直就像梦想成真一样。

sentences.en: So there's no excuses.
sentences.zh: 所以没有借口了。

sentences.en: Go give it a read.
sentences.zh: 去读一读吧。

sentences.en: I think it will be quite validating, quite illuminating as well.
sentences.zh: 我认为这会非常有说服力，也很有启发性。

sentences.en: Okay, the second question we got was, how do I navigate early dating during PMS?
sentences.zh: 好的，我们收到的第二个问题是，在PMS期间如何处理早期的约会？

sentences.en: Now, this is tough because we talked about how PMS sometimes promotes, encourages,
sentences.zh: 这很棘手，因为我们讨论过PMS有时如何促进、鼓励、

sentences.en: creates a lot of interpersonal tension just because we are coming to the table feeling a little bit different in ourselves,
sentences.zh: 制造大量的人际紧张，仅仅是因为我们带着一种对自己感觉有点不同的状态来到对方面前，

sentences.en: perhaps less patient, perhaps less patient, perhaps more sensitive.
sentences.zh: 也许耐心更少，也许更敏感。

sentences.en: And so when you first started dating someone, sometimes you don't always want to present that version of yourself that maybe you feel a little bit ashamed of.
sentences.zh: 所以当你刚开始和某人约会时，有时你并不总是想展示那个你可能感到有点羞耻的自己。

sentences.en: You have no reason to, but maybe you're like, oh, you know, dating is anxiety inducing enough.
sentences.zh: 你没有理由感到羞耻，但也许你会想，哦，你知道，约会本身就已经够让人焦虑的了。

sentences.en: Then put in my PMS or my PMDD symptoms and like it's just a freaking hurricane of reactivity and not knowing what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 再加上我的PMS或PMDD症状，简直就是一场该死的反应飓风，让人不知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: So I think you have two options based on how you want to go about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为根据你想采取的方式，你有两个选择。

sentences.en: The first path is slow and cautious.
sentences.zh: 第一条路是缓慢而谨慎。

sentences.en: The second is all in.
sentences.zh: 第二条路是全力以赴。

sentences.en: So with the first path, we are going to consciously take back time for ourself during our period and not communicate why that is with someone else.
sentences.zh: 对于第一条路，我们要在经期有意识地为自己留出时间，并且不向对方解释原因。

sentences.en: So if they're not your partner, if it's early dating, you might not want to let them in.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们还不是你的伴侣，如果只是早期约会，你可能不想让他们介入。

sentences.en: You might not want them to know what is going on because dating can be stressful.
sentences.zh: 你可能不想让他们知道发生了什么，因为约会可能会有压力。

sentences.en: PMS can be stressful, especially if you are worried about someone's approval or judgment of it.
sentences.zh: PMS可能会有压力，特别是如果你担心某人的认可或对它的评判时。

sentences.en: So only engage with this person when you feel like it.
sentences.zh: 所以，只在你感觉想的时候与这个人互动。

sentences.en: Try and pull back a little bit for that period just for your own self-care.
sentences.zh: 为了自我关怀，试着在那段时期稍微退后一点。

sentences.en: But also remember that you can't say the wrong thing to the right person.
sentences.zh: 但也要记住，对于对的人，你永远不会说错话。

sentences.en: They will understand.
sentences.zh: 他们会理解的。

sentences.en: They will reciprocate or give, you know, give you grace and be generous and kind if you do tell them.
sentences.zh: 如果你告诉他们，他们会给予回应，或者说，会体谅你，对你宽容友善。

sentences.en: And that is option two.
sentences.zh: 这就是第二个选择。

sentences.en: Option one, you tell them later down the line, you spend those first three months.
sentences.zh: 第一个选择是，你以后再告诉他们，先自己度过那最初的三个月。

sentences.en: You know, managing your PMS on your own as you have been accustomed to.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，像往常一样自己应对经前综合征（PMS）。

sentences.en: Or you can just be up front.
sentences.zh: 或者你也可以直接坦白。

sentences.en: You can be straight up and just say, hey, I'm going to be kind of out for the count this week.
sentences.zh: 你可以开门见山地说，嘿，这周我可能状态不太好。

sentences.en: I've got really bad PMS and I don't really want to be around people.
sentences.zh: 我经前综合征很严重，不太想见人。

sentences.en: Is that OK?
sentences.zh: 这样可以吗？

sentences.en: Do you understand?
sentences.zh: 你能理解吗？

sentences.en: It's probably a very good litmus test as well as to whether someone will make a good partner.
sentences.zh: 这可能也是衡量一个人是否适合做伴侣的绝佳试金石。

sentences.en: If they can respond positively or appropriately to you telling them about this medical condition you have and how it makes your life more difficult.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能对你告知的这种身体状况，以及它如何让你生活变得更艰难的情况，做出积极或恰当的回应。

sentences.en: OK, question number three.
sentences.zh: 好的，第三个问题。

sentences.en: Why do I want to rage at everyone?
sentences.zh: 为什么我总想对所有人发火？

sentences.en: I mentioned this a couple of times, but we didn't speak about it in depth, which is totally an oversight for me.
sentences.zh: 我提过几次，但没深入探讨，这确实是我的疏忽。

sentences.en: Because rage, anger, frustration, fury is a huge component of PMs.
sentences.zh: 因为愤怒、恼火、挫败感和狂怒是经前综合征的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: Why is it this case?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样呢？

sentences.en: Well, estrogen in particular plays, obviously, as we know, a key role in supporting serotonin, which is the happy hormone.
sentences.zh: 嗯，众所周知，雌激素在支持血清素（即快乐荷尔蒙）方面起着关键作用。

sentences.en: It also helps stabilize our mood.
sentences.zh: 它也有助于稳定我们的情绪。

sentences.en: So estrogen drops, serotonin drops, mood swings, low patience, irritability all ensue.
sentences.zh: 所以雌激素下降，血清素随之下降，情绪波动、耐心不足、易怒便接踵而至。

sentences.en: At times as well, because progesterone induces a calming effect when that is lower, you know, there is less of that anti-anxiety counterbalance.
sentences.zh: 有时，因为孕酮具有镇静作用，当它降低时，那种抗焦虑的平衡作用就减弱了。

sentences.en: So it throws your nervous system off balance and increases your sensitivity to stress and to frustration and to small mistakes that to you blow up in your mind because your brain is just dealing with a lot right now.
sentences.zh: 这会扰乱你的神经系统，增加你对压力、挫折以及小错误的敏感度，这些小错误在你的脑海中会被放大，因为你的大脑此刻正承受着巨大的压力。

sentences.en: You may also find that your window for tolerance is a lot smaller.
sentences.zh: 你可能还会发现自己的容忍度变低了。

sentences.en: Like the little things that you would normally look past are so frustrating and so irritating.
sentences.zh: 就像那些平时你会忽略的小事，现在却让你感到如此沮丧和恼火。

sentences.en: There is some evidence to actually suggest that the amygdala, which is the brain's emotional alarm system,
sentences.zh: 有一些证据表明，大脑的情绪警报系统——杏仁核，

sentences.en: is a lot more reactive during this time before and just as your period begins as well.
